misconceptions.constant-to-1: A constant's derivative is 0, not 1: it doesn't change.
misconceptions.dropped-inner: Multiply by the derivative of the inside: that's what the chain rule adds.
misconceptions.dropped-second-term: That's only f′g. The product rule has two terms: f′g + fg′.
misconceptions.exponent-unchanged: Bring the power down and also subtract 1 from it.
misconceptions.forgot-square: The denominator is squared: g², not g.
misconceptions.power-up: The power rule lowers the exponent by one: n xⁿ⁻¹, not n xⁿ⁺¹.
misconceptions.product-of-derivatives: The derivative of a product isn't the product of derivatives. Each factor takes its turn: f′g + fg′.
misconceptions.quotient-of-derivatives: Dividing the derivatives doesn't work. Use (f′g − fg′)/g².
misconceptions.quotient-order: The order on top is f′g − fg′ (derivative of the top first). Swapping them flips the sign.
misconceptions.wrong-rule: Picked a rule that doesn't match the outermost structure.

outcome: Differentiate using the sum, constant-multiple, power, product, quotient and chain rules.
